study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are clearly stated: to map normative development/aging of the cerebellum and apply normative models to independent clinical samples to examine heterogeneity and associations with cognition. The purpose of normative modeling is explicitly described (quantify individual deviations relative to population norms and study clinical heterogeneity). Both listed criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "we mapped the normative development and aging of the cerebellum across the lifespan using brain scans of >54,000 participants." ... "Applying the normative models in independent samples revealed substantial heterogeneity within five clinical illnesses... Finally, extreme deviations were associated with cognitive scores."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model. Eligibility/data completeness and QC standards are described (ENIGMA Cerebellum QC, ACAPULCO QC, manual inspection ~5%). Exclusion rules are specified (outliers in ≥2 regions; sites with <5 participants; withdrawn; missing demographics or T1). Final sample sizes for reference cohort are provided overall and by partition (Table 1; TR=27,117; TE=26,985).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Participants who had withdrawn from the studies or had missing demographic information and T1-weighted MRI data were excluded from the analyses." ... "We executed quality control by running the ENIGMA Cerebellum Volumetric Pipeline QC Scripts... We excluded participants if their scans denoted outliers in at least 2 regions and if each scanning-site had fewer than 5 participants... This division resulted in 27,117 individuals in TR and 26,985 individuals in TE."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are included as covariates. Multi-site effects are addressed by controlling/correcting for scanning site and treating site as a fixed effect in the model.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "All normative models included age and sex as covariates, while controlling for scanning-site-related variability." ... "predicting ... on the basis of sex and age, while correcting for scanning site... To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources for the reference cohort are clearly listed, including named public datasets and number of scanning sites.

ADNI..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "The cohort of individuals without diagnoses was obtained from 132 scanning sites, including various studies such as ABIDE... UK Biobank... ADNI..."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and pipelines are described: FreeSurfer 5.3, FSL (reorient, flirt), N4 bias correction, ANTs registration to ICBM 2009c, ACAPULCO v0.2.1 for lobular parcellation with QC and outlier removal, and SUIT v3.4 for voxel-level segmentation with Jacobian modulation.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The T1-weighted images were skull stripped using the FreeSurfer 5.3 auto-recon pipeline... fslreorient2std... flirt... default 1 mm FSL template..."; "we utilized the ACAPULCO version 0.2.1... automated quality control... removed the extreme outliers..."; "we utilized the SUIT version 3.4... gray matter maps were normalized... modulated by the Jacobian..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Internal validation via partitioning the reference cohort into training and test sets stratified by site, sex, and age; minimum per-site sample; clinical groups only in test set for evaluation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We split our sample of individuals without diagnosis into training and test sets on the basis of scanning site, sex, and age... evenly split the control participants from each scanning site... A minimum of five participants from the same scanning site was required."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study reports a held-out test set of healthy individuals (internal validation) and applies models to independent clinical samples. It does not explicitly apply the normative model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals beyond the internal test partition assembled from the same multi-dataset pool.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We split our sample... into training and test sets..."; Figures and text describe application to clinical test samples, not to a separate external healthy dataset.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping ('sinarcsinsh'), implemented with PCNtoolkit v0.24 in Python 3.8, with site modeled as a fixed effect.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "We used the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.24) in Python 3.8... We employed a Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping... using the 'sinarcsinsh' transformation... To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is quantitatively assessed and reported using explained variance and additional metrics (kurtosis, skew, mean squared logarithmic loss) computed on the held-out test set.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we report the performance of these models, in terms of explained variance... Additional evaluation metrics such as kurtosis, skew, and mean squared logarithmic loss..."; "These evaluation metrics were computed in the test set that did not include any clinical groups."
